    🦎 Zebekyo¶

    "The hunt remembers. The scales do not lie."

    Zebekyo is the faith of the Emberalden Lizardfolk — a taller, stronger subrace of Kobolds who built a permanent nation on the Demon Continent where their smaller cousins manage only warrens. Where standard kobolds have no faith beyond survival and traps, Zebekyo gives the Emberalden a hunter's theology: the Great Hunt is prayer, prey is scripture, and every scale records a deed.

    The name Zebekyo comes from the old kobold tongue: zebek ("scale-that-holds") + yo ("way" or "road") — the way of the scale that holds.

    Origins¶

    Zebekyo emerged after the Emberalden split from the kobold warrens and settled the sun-warmed flats northwest of Blazeyard. Freed from tunnel-dark and trap-anxiety, the taller lizardfolk began to hunt in the open — and to ask why some hunts succeed and others fail in ways that skill alone could not explain.

    The first Zebekyo teaching is attributed to Scar-Throat Vekka, a hunt-leader who tracked a shadow-cat for nine days in the Age 8 wastes and returned with its skull, claiming the beast had allowed itself to be taken because the hunt had been "true." Her account — recited at every Great Hunt since — became the seed of the faith: prey and hunter are partners in a rite that the land itself judges.

    Zebekyo does not claim a divine founder. It claims that the hunt itself is the teacher, and Vekka was merely the first to listen well.

    Beliefs¶

    • The hunt is liturgy — every stage of the hunter's sequence (track → stalk → strike → return → share) is a sacred office. To rush a stage is sacrilege; to skip one is to hunt without the land's permission.
    • Scales hold debts — an Emberalden's scales are believed to darken subtly with each worthy kill and pale with each wasteful one. Elders "read" a youth's hide before approving their solo rite. This is partly myth, partly the real way scales scar and stain with diet and sun.
    • Zebek — the First Scale — a mythic ur-kobold whose every scale was a flawless hunting record. Some tales say Zebek grew until its scales became Emberalden's stone flats; others say it still walks the savanna at night, judging hunts.
    • No temples, but kill-circles — Zebekyo has no closed buildings. Its holy sites are open-air rings of predator skulls (kill-circles) where the year's Great Hunt is opened and closed with chants that list every species taken fairly.
    • Sharing is absolution — meat kept is meat wasted in the spiritual sense. A hunter who does not share the kill with clan, hatchlings, and even rival clans has not completed the rite.

    Practices¶

    • Solo skull rite — at ~14 years, every Emberalden must hunt alone and return with a predator skull (not scavenged) to be recognized as adult. Failure is not exile — the youth may try again each season until they succeed; persistence is itself a valued sign.
    • Great Hunt — an annual week-long communal hunt whose order of precedence determines social standing for the year ahead. The clan-mother or strongest hunter leads, but "strength" is measured in clean hunts: efficient, minimal-suffering kills with full use of the carcass.
    • Scale-reading — elders examine a hunter's neck and shoulder scales under midday sun to assess their year. Dark, even coloration is praised; bleached or patchy tones prompt counseling or fasting hunts.
    • Bone-craft as prayer — tools, amulets, and dwelling ornaments carved from bone are made with chants naming the animal, the hunt date, and the hunter's intent. A well-made bone knife is a minor relic.

    Relation to Other Faiths¶

    Zebekyo is local and non-proselytizing. It does not compete with Kirivs-bin or Malgardism — many Emberalden who trade with Malgardian Tribe and Blazeyard attend Malgardist shrines or respect the bin without contradiction. In Emberalden itself, however, Zebekyo is universal and unchallenged.

    The Asatru Empire, which trades for Emberalden leather and bone-craft, officially classifies Zebekyo as a "hunt custom" rather than a religion — a diplomatic fiction that lets both sides avoid theological debate while doing business.

    Influence¶

    • Majority: Emberalden — universal among the lizardfolk; the faith and the nation are inseparable
    • Minority: small kobold-blooded enclaves along the Emberalden–Malgardian border who have adopted Zebekyo alongside warren-survival habits
    • Heavily respected by Malgardian Tribe hunters (who sometimes seek Emberalden "scale-reading" before major expeditions) and tolerated by Blazeyard Flames as "a fireless way of being precise"
    • Standard Kobolds in tunnels regard Zebekyo with awe and resentment — proof that their kin can build something they cannot
